Cleveland |asst_coach3=[[Scotty Thurman]] |stadium=[[Bud Walton Arena]] |tourney=[[2019 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |tourney_result = Second Round |assoc_coach=[[Melvin Watkins]] |ahc_year= }} {{2018–19 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2018–19 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arkansas]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by eighth-year head coach [[Mike Anderson (basketball, born 1959)|Mike Anderson]], and played their home games at [[Bud Walton Arena]] in [[Fayetteville, Arkansas]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 18–16, 8–10 in [[2018–19 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC Play]] to finish a tie for 9th place. They lost in the Second Round of the [[2019 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] to [[2018–19 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they defeated [[2018–19 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the First Round before losing in the Second Round to [[2018–19 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]]. On March 26, 2019, Arkansas athletic director [[Hunter Yurachek]] fired Anderson. ==Previous season== Arkansas finished the season 23–12, 10–8 in SEC play to finish in a three-way tie for fourth place. As the No. 6 seed in the [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], the Razorbacks defeated [[2017–18 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020005|title=South Carolina vs. Arkansas - Game Recap - March 8, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-06-29}} and [[2017–18 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/college/florida/article/florida-gators-basketball-loses-to-arkansas-razorbacks-shoots-a-blank-ducks-out-of-sec-tournament-116053109/|title=Florida Gators Basketball loses to Arkansas Razorbacks, shoots a blank, ducks out of SEC Tournament|work=Swamp247|access-date=2018-06-29|language=en-US}} before losing in the semifinals to [[2017–18 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020011|title=Arkansas vs. Tennessee - Game Recap - March 10, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-06-29}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2017–18 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025827|title=Butler vs. Arkansas - Game Recap - March 16, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-06-29}} Senior guard Jaylen Barford was named first team All-SEC, while senior guard Daryl Macon was a second team All-SEC selection. Freshman center Daniel Gafford was named to the SEC All-Freshman Team.{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/article/3-arkansas-razorbacks-honored-named-to-coaches-all-sec-teams-jaylen-barford-daryl-macon-daniel-gafford-115898207/|title=3 Arkansas Razorbacks honored named to coaches' All-SEC teams - Jaylen Barford, Daryl Macon, Daniel Gafford|work=HawgSports.com|access-date=2018-06-29|language=en-US}} On March 26, 2018, Gafford announced he would forgo the 2018 NBA draft, and would be returning to Arkansas for his sophomore season.{{Cite news|url=http://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2018/mar/26/daniel-gafford-will-return-arkansas-sophomore-seas/|title=Daniel Gafford will return to Arkansas for sophomore season|date=2018-03-26|work=Arkansas Online|access-date=2018-06-29|language=en}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
